authored_files.content: bounded-scale bridge: separated-set, packing-number, covering-number and explicit-cover bounds; scalingConstantOf form and explicit-ratio form

finite discrete models Disc n with counting measure; uniform doubling constant 1; coveringNumber eps univ = n for eps < 1; isometry measure transfer; member-level doubling measures; GHSpace family with uniform diameter 1; failure of uniformCovers at every radius below 1; not totally bounded
Borel structure on GHSpace.Rep; uniformCovers_of_ratio_data; gromovCriterion and gh_subseq_of_uniformCovers consumption; counterexample corollaries with member-level measures
unconditional numeric instance on R: coveringNumber 1 (closedBall 0 1) <= 12

sharpness of the ratio hypothesis: on Disc n, uniform ratio data at the large-to-small scale pair forces n <= C (card_le_of_uniform_ratio); counting measure attains C = n (count_ratio_data_sharp); at every scale 0 < eps < 2 no constants satisfy the ratio data of uniformCovers_of_ratio_data on discreteFamily (not_uniformRatioData_discreteFamily_at, with the eps = 1/4 specialization not_uniformRatioData_discreteFamily); the full hypothesis bundle of uniformCovers_of_ratio_data is false for discreteFamily (uniformCovers_of_ratio_data_hypothesis_fails); for every M and eps < 1 there is a doubling space of diameter <= 1 with coveringNumber eps > M (exists_doubling_coveringNumber_gt)
fail-closed per-declaration kernel axiom audit over 60 declarations

limitations: uniformCovers_of_ratio_data / isCompact_of_ratio_data / gh_subseq_of_ratio_data are conditional: the uniform ball-ratio constants and the non-collapse inequalities are hypotheses. Deriving them from curvature bounds + non-collapsing (Bishop-Gromov) is not done here.

A family-level statement phrased with numerical bounds on scalingConstantOf is not instantiable: scalingConstantOf is Classical.choose-based, so its value is opaque; this is why the consumption theorem uses explicit ratio constants.

The counterexample refutes the unrestricted implication (uniform local doubling + uniform diameter => uniform covers). It does not refute the conditional family theorem; on the contrary, Sharpness.lean proves that at every scale 0 < eps < 2 the discrete family fails exactly the ratio hypothesis of uniformCovers_of_ratio_data (not_uniformRatioData_discreteFamily_at, uniformCovers_of_ratio_data_hypothesis_fails), and it remains consistent with the bounded-scale bridge: at radius r with a positive finite reference mass the bridge applies.
U9 remains open: no curvature => doubling/non-collapse input is provided, so Cheeger-Gromov compactness for Riemannian families is still not available.

verdict_detail: No named blocker is closed. The measure-to-cover subproblem of U9 is settled at bounded scale, the unrestricted form is refuted, and the failure is localized to the ratio/non-collapse hypothesis, which must diverge along the family. The missing U9 input (curvature/non-collapsing => uniform ball-ratio data, Bishop-Gromov) is not constructed.
verdict_scope: Acceptance milestone met: (a) a proved bounded-scale bridge from mathlib's IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure + scalingConstantOf to covering-number bounds for balls, in both scalingConstantOf and explicit-ratio form; (b) a proved counterexample family showing that the uniformly-local hypothesis plus a uniform diameter bound is insufficient for the D12 uniform-cover hypothesis; (c) the counterexample is provably sharp: at every scale below the diameter it fails exactly the ratio hypothesis of the conditional consumption theorem, and the required constant is at least the number of points (n <= C, attained at C = n); (d) consumption of the bridge in D12 gromovCriterion/uniformCovers with constructed input and checked downstream use; (e) every declaration classified. Not a Poincare proof; U9 open.
